blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: In [@HatcherOertel], Hatcher and Oertel gave an algorithm for computing the boundary slopes of a Montesinos knot. At the end of their paper they provided a table giving the boundary slopes for each Montesinos knot in the standard table in Rolfsen's book [@Rolfsen76]. Unfortunately, their table contains several (17) errors. These errors were due to problems with the computer program that generated the table, as well as transcription/printing errors. This note provides a corrected table which was generated by a completely new computer program. Section [\[table\]](#table){reference-type="ref" ref

blocks.title: Preparing the table
blocks.content:
[]{#method label="method"}

In this section I briefly describe the precautions taken to insure that the table in Section [\[table\]](#table){reference-type="ref" reference="table"} is correct. I first noticed errors in the table in [@HatcherOertel] when comparing it with the output of a program that computes the *normal* boundary slopes of a knot (that is, the boundary slopes of all surfaces which are normal with respect to a choice of triangulation of the exterior of the knot). blocks.title: Getting the program
blocks.content:
[]{#gettingprogram label="gettingprogram"}

The programs I used in preparing this note are available at <http://dunfield.info/montesinos>. They are written the programming language Python, and you will need a Python interpreter to run them. These interpreters are available, for free and for almost all platforms, from <http://python.org>.
